messages:
alex_m: Quick sync — we need to lock GA acceptance criteria for the new 'workload-aware batching' initiative by EOD Friday. I sketched a minimal set: SLA, docs, support runbook, monitoring, and pricing examples. Who can own each?
marie-p: I can take SLA + docs. Do we have baseline numbers from the pilot? need p50/p95 and error-rate targets.
samir: Ops here — I’ll own support/runbook handoff. Need confirmation on oncall routing and rollback triggers. Also: do we require a dedicated playbook for Dedicated customers?
oliver_k: Monitoring / observability checklist:
- define KPIs: p50, p95, 99, request error %, cold-start errors
- traces attached to request ids
- metric tags: model, quant-mode, batch-size
- pager thresholds + runbook links

Proposed alert thresholds (draft):
```
alerts:
  high_error_rate: error_rate > 0.5% for 5m
  latency_p95: p95 > 500ms for 10m
  degraded_throughput: tokens_per_gpu < 60% baseline for 15m
```
jenna: Pricing/finops here — we need 3 public examples (low, mid, high throughput) with cost per 1M tokens and a short explanation of batching/quantization impact. I can produce those if engineering gives perf numbers.
alex_m: Good. For SLA language, aim for something simple and testable. Marie, can you draft something like this and we’ll iterate?
marie-p: Drafting now. Initial SLA snippet: 
```
SLA:
  availability: 99.9% monthly uptime
  latency_p95: <= 300ms (short payloads), <= 800ms (long sequences)
  error_rate: < 0.5%
  support_response: P1 within 15m, P2 within 2h
```
Thoughts?
samir: Fine but clarify scope: hosted API only vs Dedicated/Private. Recommend default SLA applies to hosted; Dedicated customers get contractual SLAs with capacity commitment. Add that to the draft.
oliver_k: Agree on scope callout. Also add monitoring SLOs and synthetic checks (end-to-end smoke every 5m). We should define a synthetic prompt set (10 prompts) for latency/quality regression.
jenna: Pricing note: for public examples, we need two variants per example (with and without prefix caching). That affects unit cost a lot.
marie-p: Added scope clause and synthetic checks note to the doc. uploaded: https://docs.redwood.internal/launch/workload-batching/ga-sla-draft (please review).
ops-bot: runbook: /ops/runbooks/workload-batching-ga v0.2 uploaded by samir — diff: +support-routing.md, +rollback-checks.md
alex_m: Owners recap: SLA & docs = marie-p; Support/runbook = samir; Monitoring = oliver_k; Pricing examples = jenna. Action items before EOD Fri:
- marie-p: publish SLA + acceptance tests (unit + e2e synthetic)
- samir: finalize support runbook, oncall routing, and dedicated handoff notes
- oliver_k: commit dashboards + alerts, synthetic job config in CI
- jenna: send 3 pricing examples once perf numbers are posted
Any other gaps?
samir: Need explicit rollback plan on capacity failures — i.e., fallback to smaller model variant and routing policy. I'll draft steps.
marie-p: Also we should decide doc visibility (public vs customers-only). Recommend public FAQ + customers-only runbook for Dedicated details.
oliver_k: One more: add automated regression alert that ties to prompt-set evaluation when new model/quant changes are rolled out.
jenna: acked. I’ll wait for perf numbers from eng-runtime.
alex_m: Great. If no objections, I’ll mark this as the canonical GA checklist and mention owners in the product release doc. Please add short PRs/links into the thread so we can close by EOD Fri. :thumbsup:
